answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to escrow a bond before it may transact, then randomly audit its signed work and slash the bond for fabricated results or collusion. One honest operator can reuse a trusted identity, while a Sybil attacker must lock capital for every fake identity and expose each one to audits; scaling the attack therefore raises cost linearly. A grove may grow at dawn around one honest root, but each fake branch still pays the inlet fee.
